title: Phase 0: chapter list/detail view with edit & delete
description: Property dashboard listing chapters (filter by type/status). Chapter detail view: photo grid, edit chapter title/description/type, delete chapter, edit/delete individual photos, reassign a photo to a different chapter. This is the 'basic organization' + 'ease of editing' piece Pete specifically wants to validate first.
close_reason: Chapter detail view built (chapter.html): edit title/category/description/status, delete chapter (unfiles its photos back to pending_review rather than deleting them), photo grid with per-photo description edit, move-to-another-chapter, and delete. Chapter list in app.html now links to it. Verified end-to-end in browser with throwaway test data: edit+save, move between chapters, delete chapter unfiling confirmed, and confirmed unfiled photo resurfaces correctly in upload.html's needs-review queue.

title: Phase 0: review/confirm UI before saving AI suggestions
description: After Claude analyzes uploaded photos, show its suggested chapter_type/title/description/extracted fields and let the user edit any of it before confirming. On confirm: either create a new chapter or attach to an existing open one. This is the core 'won't get it right the first time' safety valve — must be fast, not a big form.
close_reason: Review/confirm UI built into upload.html: editable chapter_type/title/description/fields, create-new-chapter or attach-to-existing-chapter, photo thumbnail shown. Also added a 'needs review' section that resurfaces previously-uploaded-but-unconfirmed photos (found and preserved Pete's own real test photo this way). Verified end-to-end in browser: both save paths tested at the data level.

title: Phase 0: Claude Vision analysis edge function
description: Edge Function that takes pending media (+ any user note) and calls Claude to produce: suggested chapter_type, title, description, and type-specific extracted fields (e.g. paint color name/code if a paint can, brand/model if an appliance is visible). For a batch upload, propose whether photos form one chapter with a timeline. Store result on media.ai_description/ai_extracted, don't auto-create the chapter yet — that's the review step's job.
close_reason: analyze-media edge function deployed: runs under caller's own JWT (no service-role bypass), downloads photo, calls Claude with a forced tool-use categorize_photo call, stores suggestion on the media row. Verified end-to-end in browser.

title: Phase 0: photo capture/upload UI (single + batch)

Must support the batch-upload case (dozens of renovation photos at once) as well as single quick captures (one paint can photo). Stores to Storage + creates media rows with status=pending_review, chapter_id null until AI/review step assigns one.
close_reason: Upload UI built: single+batch file input, optional batch note, uploads to houstory-media storage + creates media rows, triggers analysis, renders suggestions.

Hide chapter_type/Category everywhere it's currently shown or asked for: chapter.html's edit form (Category select), upload.html's 'File into a chapter' new-chapter fields (Category select) and the '(category)' suffix shown next to each existing chapter in that dropdown, and the main page's new-chapter form (houstory-96t.33/.34) and chapter list. There: (a) a form to add a new chapter (name + category, though category may be hidden per houstory-96t.35), (b) a list of ALL existing chapters (not just the fixed starting 8) with the ability to edit or delete each - edit can likely just link out to chapter.html's existing edit form rather than reimplementing it, delete could either happen inline here or also link out. close_reason: app.html now shows chapters as buttons (styled links to chapter.html) instead of a text list. Buttons sort in that canonical order first, with any other existing chapters (Pete's pre-existing Kitchen Appliances/Kitchen Renovation/Paint Colors) sorted alphabetically after. Renamed 'Analyze photos' to 'Add'. Dropped the '(active)'/category suffix entirely from the button labels. Inline chapter-creation form left in place for now (not yet moved to Manage Chapters - that's houstory-96t.34, not part of this bead). Verified end-to-end in browser: correct order, correct styling, clicking a button navigates to the right chapter.

title: Consolidate 'file into chapter' into one Unfiled section, remove it from every chapter page
description: chapter.html's 'Add existing unfiled photos' picker currently shows ALL of the property's unfiled photos at the bottom of EVERY chapter's page - the same list duplicated across every chapter, confusing/redundant. Fix: (a) remove that section from chapter.html entirely - stop showing unfiled photos there; (b) build out upload.html's existing 'Unfiled' gallery (already collapsed-by-default per houstory-96t.31) into the one place this happens - each unfiled group gets a 'File into a chapter' action: pick an existing chapter from a dropdown, or create a new chapter (name + category) right there, then move that group's photos into it. Collapsed-by-default in this section per Pete's explicit ask. Reuses the create-chapter pattern already on app.html (houstory-96t) and the dropdown-of-existing-chapters pattern already on chapter.html's merge feature (houstory-96t.21).
notes: Found during testing: filing one unfiled group into a brand-new chapter didn't make that chapter appear in OTHER already-rendered unfiled cards' dropdowns, since their <select> HTML was built before the new chapter existed. Fixing by reloading the whole Unfiled list after a successful file, rather than just removing the one card.
close_reason: Removed the 'Add existing unfiled photos' picker from chapter.html entirely (was showing the same unfiled photos duplicated at the bottom of every chapter). upload.html's existing Unfiled section (already collapsed-by-default) is now the one place this happens: each unfiled group gets a 'File into a chapter' dropdown (existing chapters + 'Create new chapter' with name/category fields) and a File button. Filing reloads the Unfiled list so newly-created chapters immediately become available as targets for OTHER still-unfiled groups too. Verified end-to-end: filed one group into a brand-new chapter, filed a second group into that same now-existing chapter, confirmed chapter.html shows both photos with no unfiled section present.

title: Group unfiled photos from the same submission, and allow deleting them
description: Uploading 2+ photos together (one submission, one shared Claude response) currently shows them as separate cards in the 'Unfiled' gallery, each repeating the identical description - confusing, looks like duplicate/redundant entries. Fix: add media.upload_batch_id (set once client-side per submission), group the Unfiled display by it so one submission = one card with all its thumbnails + one shared description. Also add a Delete action per unfiled group (with a confirm() dialog) since there was previously no way to remove an unfiled photo without filing it into a chapter first.
close_reason: Added media.upload_batch_id (set once client-side per submission, migration 006). Unfiled gallery now groups by batch id: one submission = one card with all its thumbnails + one shared description, instead of repeating the description per photo. Added a Delete button per unfiled group with a confirm() dialog, removing all its media rows and storage objects. Verified end-to-end: a 2-photo submission grouped into one card with one description; delete removed both rows from the database. Older pre-migration entries correctly fall back to showing individually (no batch id to group by).

title: Large phone photos crash analyze-media with HTTP 546 (edge function resource limit)
description: Pete submitted 2 real phone-camera photos of the range together (2.0MB + 4.3MB JPEGs) and got 'Analysis failed: HTTP 546' - not an error our own code returns, so this is the Supabase edge-runtime terminating the worker for exceeding a resource limit (memory or CPU time) while downloading+base64-encoding+submitting ~8MB of combined image data to Claude in one invocation. A single smaller photo (paint can) worked fine. Fix: resize/compress images client-side before upload (e.g. cap at ~1568px longest edge, matching Claude's own effective vision resolution anyway, so no analysis quality is lost) rather than uploading/processing full-resolution originals. This also reduces storage costs and upload time.
acceptance_criteria: Photos are resized/re-encoded client-side (canvas, capped ~1568px longest edge, JPEG ~0.85 quality) before upload in upload.html, skipping resize if already smaller. Verified multi-photo submissions of realistically-sized images no longer hit the resource limit.
close_reason: Fixed by resizing images client-side before upload (canvas, capped at 1568px longest edge, JPEG q=0.85) - matches Claude's own effective vision resolution so no analysis quality is lost. Verified: a synthetic 4032x3024 (typical phone camera resolution) image resizes correctly to 1568x1176, and a 2-photo submission at that resolution (which reproduces the same data volume that crashed with HTTP 546) now completes successfully with no error.

title: Submitting a photo crashed with 'null is not an object (evaluating user.id)' on stale session
description: Pete hit this on his phone submitting a new photo via upload.html. Root cause: several places called sb.auth.getUser() and used the result's .id without checking it existed. getUser() validates whatever access token is currently in memory and fails outright if it's stale - it does NOT auto-refresh. On mobile, Safari suspends timers while the page is backgrounded, so a scheduled token auto-refresh can miss its window, leaving a stale token by the time you come back and submit something.
acceptance_criteria: Fixed by using sb.auth.getSession() instead everywhere a current user is needed - getSession() auto-refreshes an expired access token as long as the refresh token is still valid. Added a shared requireSession() helper (in upload.html and app.html) that redirects to login.html gracefully if the session is truly gone, instead of crashing. Verified in browser: corrupting the stored session causes a clean redirect to sign-in rather than a crash; normal submission still works.
close_reason: Fixed: getUser() calls replaced with getSession() (auto-refreshes) via a shared requireSession() helper in upload.html and app.html, with a graceful redirect-to-login fallback instead of crashing. Verified both the corrupted-session redirect path and normal submission in browser.

title: Simplify to a freeform analyze playground: photos + instructions, no forced categorization
description: Pivot away from the rigid categorize_photo tool schema and chapter-target UI in the upload flow. New model: upload.html becomes select 1+ photos, write freeform instructions for Claude, submit, see the raw response - no chapter_type/title/fields extraction forced at submission time. Photos save unfiled (chapter_id null, status pending_review) with the raw response stored on ai_description; organizing into a chapter becomes a separate, later, deliberate step. Requires: analyze-media simplified to a single path (any number of media_ids, freeform instructions text, no tool_choice forcing); app.html gets a 'create new chapter' form since that capability is being removed from upload.html; chapter.html gets an 'add existing unfiled photos' picker so analyzed-but-unfiled photos can be filed later. Rationale (Pete, 2026-08-01): got caught up in categorization UI instead of being able to freely tune how Claude analyzes photos - wants a lower-friction way to iterate on instructions/wording before re-engaging with structured extraction.
close_reason: Rebuilt upload.html as a freeform playground: pick 1+ photos, write instructions, submit, see Claude's raw text response - no forced chapter_type/title/fields extraction. analyze-media simplified to one path (any number of media_ids + instructions, no tool_choice forcing). Photos save unfiled; app.html gained a manual 'create new chapter' form (moved out of the old upload flow); chapter.html gained an 'add existing unfiled photos' picker (multi-select, also covers houstory-96t.14). Verified end-to-end: created a chapter via the new form, submitted a photo with custom instructions and got a detailed unconstrained response, filed it into the chapter via the new picker, confirmed the unfiled list correctly shrank. This also superseded houstory-96t.16 (closed) and re-scoped houstory-96t.17/96t.18/96t.22 (notes added).

title: Detect/prevent near-duplicate chapters (e.g. 'Appliances' vs 'Kitchen Appliances' vs 'Kitchen Remodel Appliances')
description: Found while investigating houstory-96t.20: Pete's property now has 3 separate appliance chapters ('Appliances', 'Kitchen Appliances', 'Kitchen Remodel Appliances') because each independent photo analysis invents its own suggested_chapter_name with no awareness of chapters that already exist. When creating a new chapter, compare the suggested name against the property's existing open chapters (by name similarity and/or matching chapter_type) and nudge toward attaching to an existing one instead of silently allowing near-duplicates to pile up. Related open question worth raising with Pete rather than deciding unilaterally: should each individual appliance get its own chapter (e.g. 'Fulgor Range', 'Bosch Dishwasher'), or should there be one shared 'Kitchen Appliances' bucket for all of them? Current behavior is inconsistent on this.
notes: Risk further reduced after Pete declared a fixed starting taxonomy (houstory-96t.33: Appliances/Paint/Projects/Contractors/Iconic Photos/Materials/Landscaping/Repairs) plus a centralized 'Manage Chapters' add/edit/delete flow (houstory-96t.34) instead of ad hoc inline creation. Still possible to create a near-duplicate by hand there, but far less likely now. Consider closing this as low-priority/superseded once .33/.34 ship, unless it's still happening in practice.

title: Merge two chapters into one
description: Recovery feature for when photos of the same item end up split across chapters (e.g. missed grouping - houstory-96t.20, or independently-created near-duplicate chapters - houstory-96t.21). Let the user pick a source and target chapter and move all the source's photos into the target, then delete (or archive) the now-empty source. Natural home for this is chapter.html - e.g. a 'Merge into another chapter...' action alongside the existing delete.
close_reason: Merge feature built in chapter.html: pick another chapter from a dropdown, confirm, and all photos move there; metadata is shallow-merged (target's values win on conflict), description falls back to the source's if the target has none, and the now-empty source chapter is deleted with a redirect to the surviving target. Verified end-to-end with throwaway test chapters: photo moved, metadata merged correctly, source deleted, redirected to target.

title: Grouping step is too easy to miss - photos of one item end up in separate chapters
description: Real-world test: Pete uploaded a range's front photo + its data-plate photo in one batch, expecting them grouped (houstory-96t.15), but neither went through the group path - confirmed via ai_extracted lacking group_media_ids on both rows. Both got analyzed independently and landed in 2 different chapters ('Kitchen Appliances' vs 'Kitchen Remodel Appliances'). Root cause: grouping requires an extra manual step (check boxes, click 'Group selected as one item') before the main upload button, which is easy to skip or not notice, especially on mobile where the picker flow doesn't naturally cue you back to it. Needs a UX fix - options to weigh: (a) when 2+ files are selected, actively prompt 'are these views of the same item?' before letting Upload proceed, rather than a passive optional section; (b) auto-suggest grouping when file count is small (2-4) and there's one shared batch note; (c) something else. Don't just make it more visible - make it hard to accidentally skip.
close_reason: Fixed by gating the Upload button rather than just making grouping more visible: for 2+ selected files, Upload stays disabled until the user explicitly answers 'are any of these the same item?' (Yes reveals the group-checkbox UI, No just proceeds with a visible 'uploading as separate photos' note + Change link). A single file skips the gate entirely - zero added friction for the common one-photo-per-item case. Verified all paths in browser: 2-file gate blocks upload until answered, Yes/No/Change all behave correctly, single-file has no gate.

title: Per-photo title field (distinct from chapter name and description)
description: Each photo should have its own short title, separate from the chapter's title (a broader bucket name) and the photo's longer description. Useful for scanning a chapter's photo grid at a glance, and especially relevant once photos are grouped for a single item (houstory-96t.15) - e.g. two photos of one appliance might be titled 'Front of unit' and 'Model/serial sticker' while eventually sharing a merged description/fields set once grouping lands. Add media.title (nullable text), have analyze-media suggest one per photo, and expose it as an editable field in both the upload review form and the chapter detail photo grid.
close_reason: Added media.title column, analyze-media now suggests a distinct per-photo title (separate from description and suggested_chapter_name), and it's editable in both the upload review form and the chapter detail photo grid. Verified end-to-end in browser with throwaway test data.

title: Category-aware photo analysis (paint/appliance/renovation each need different extraction guidance)
description: analyze-media currently uses one generic prompt plus one catch-all 'fields: object' for every chapter_type, so Claude has no explicit instruction on what to actually look for - it defaults to a generic photo summary instead of focused extraction. E.g. a paint photo should trigger 'read the can label for brand/color name/color code/sheen', an appliance photo should trigger 'find the model/serial sticker (often on a door frame, back panel, or inside a door) and extract brand/model_number/serial_number'. Fix by giving each category its own explicit extraction guidance and/or field schema. Two implementation options to weigh: (a) one Claude call, with per-category instructions/schema selected once chapter_type is known or guessed - cheaper, faster; (b) a two-step pipeline - classify first, then a second call with a schema built specifically for that category - likely higher quality but doubles API cost/latency per photo. This is a prompt-engineering/tool-schema design task in the existing edge function, not Anthropic's Agent Skills feature (that's for packaging instructions in Claude Code/desktop apps, not applicable to a server-side Messages API call). houstory-96t.6 and houstory-96t.7 both assume this groundwork exists already - they should depend on it.
notes: Re-scoped after houstory-96t.23: users now write their own instructions per submission (e.g. 'find the model/serial sticker'), so automatic category detection is less urgent - the user already controls what Claude looks for. Might resurface later as suggested instruction templates per category, not forced extraction.

title: Manually (re-)run Claude analysis on a saved photo
description: Let the user resubmit an already-saved set of photos (a chapter's photos, or an unfiled group) for fresh analysis - reusing the same photos already in storage, including the currently-saved Claude response as context, plus new instructions the user adds now. This is a refinement/follow-up call, not a from-scratch analysis: e.g. 'you said X before, but actually...' or asking a targeted follow-up (find the manual) on an item analyzed generically before. Natural home is a button on chapter.html's photo cards and upload.html's Unfiled group cards.
notes: Still relevant after houstory-96t.23, but re-scoped: since analysis is no longer forced at upload time, 're-run analysis' now means calling analyze-media again with a media_id already in storage (no re-upload needed) and fresh instructions text - natural home is a button on chapter.html's photo cards / the unfiled picker.

title: Setting to control default Claude-analysis behavior (always/ask/never)
description: Not every photo needs AI processing, and each analysis call costs money (Anthropic API usage). Add a setting with three modes: always analyze on upload (current behavior), ask each upload whether to analyze, or never analyze automatically. 'Ask' should probably be a per-batch checkbox on the upload form (e.g. 'Analyze with Claude' checked by default) rather than a per-file prompt, since batches can be dozens of photos - open to reconsidering if that's wrong in practice. Open design question: does this setting live on the property (supabase properties table) or per-user? Simplest is a column on properties for now, revisit if/when multi-user (houstory-96t.10) makes per-user preferences matter more. When analysis is skipped, media rows still get created normally (status pending_review, ai_description/ai_extracted left null) - see houstory-96t.17 for how those get analyzed later.
close_reason: Superseded by houstory-96t.23: analysis is no longer an automatic background step to toggle on/off - submission to Claude is now always explicit (you write instructions and hit Submit), so 'always/ask/never' no longer applies.

title: Bulk-assign a batch of uploaded photos to one chapter
description: Uploading a batch of photos currently gives one independent review card per photo, each separately choosing 'create new chapter' or 'attach to existing.' For importing a folder of already-saved renovation photos (dozens at once), reviewing/assigning each one individually is tedious. Add a way to select some or all of a batch and assign them to one chapter (new or existing) in a single bulk action. Per-photo Claude analysis (each photo still gets its own ai_description) can stay as-is - this is about the save/confirm step, not the analysis step.
close_reason: Covered by houstory-96t.23: chapter.html's new 'Add existing unfiled photos' picker supports multi-select, so a whole batch of unfiled photos can be bulk-assigned to one chapter in a single action.

title: Phase 1: appliance enrichment (recalls, manuals, warranty, repair pros)
description: Enable Anthropic's web search tool in analyze-media so Claude can actually look things up when asked, instead of just describing a plausible way to find it. Real example (Pete, 2026-08-05): asked about a Fulgor Milano range, Claude suggested checking fulgor-milano.com's Support section rather than actually finding the product page/manual links; also didn't look up the named retailer (Custom Distributors, Columbus OH) or search for local repair services. With web search enabled and instructions that push toward concrete results (not just describing a search strategy), Claude should be able to surface real manual links, retailer contact info, and nearby servicer names/links directly in its response.
notes: No longer depends on houstory-96t.18 - freeform instructions (houstory-96t.23) already let the user tell Claude what it's looking at, so automatic category detection isn't a prerequisite for this.
close_reason: Enabled Anthropic's web_search_20250305 tool in analyze-media, with a system prompt nudging Claude toward concrete results (real links/contacts) over descriptions of a search strategy. Verified with Pete's actual Fulgor Milano range: a focused 'find the manual' ask returned the real manual PDF link plus the exact product page (matching what Pete found himself independently), and a focused 'find local repair services' ask returned 5 named Columbus-area businesses with phone numbers plus the nearest authorized Fulgor Milano retailer (Dayton, OH). Key finding: one focused ask per submission gets dramatically better results than bundling multiple lookups together, since Claude spreads across more searches and hedges more when asked for several things at once - added a UI hint in upload.html reflecting this.

See design discussion 2026-07-26 for full data model (properties, property_members, chapters w/ jsonb metadata, media, chapter_events, ai_credentials) and phasing.

title: Make saved-item cards collapsible/expandable
description: Chapter photo cards (chapter.html), unfiled photo groups, and live analysis results (upload.html) are always fully-expanded blocks of text/thumbnails/controls - unwieldy with several photos or a long Claude response. Add a collapsed-by-default summary (thumbnail + title/first line) that expands to the full card on click. Scope question to settle before building: which cards - just chapter photo cards, or also unfiled groups and live results? Touches the same rendering code as houstory-96t.30 (structured response formatting) - consider building together.
close_reason: Added collapsible/expandable cards using a shared card-summary/card-body pattern (thumbnail + derived title, click to expand) applied to: upload.html's live results (expanded by default, since freshly generated) and Unfiled gallery (collapsed by default), and chapter.html's photo cards (collapsed by default). chapter.html's photo description also got a view/edit toggle - rendered by default, 'Edit description' reveals the raw-text textarea, editing and saving correctly re-renders and updates the collapsed summary title. Scope: applied everywhere EXCEPT chapter.html's unfiled-photo checkbox picker, which stayed as a flat list (rendering was still added there) since a picker's rows benefit less from being individually collapsible. Verified end-to-end in browser with throwaway test data.

title: Render Claude responses with real formatting (hyperlinked URLs, bold headers) instead of raw markdown text
description: ai_description is displayed via .textContent (plain text, white-space:pre-wrap) everywhere it shows up (chapter.html photo cards, upload.html's Unfiled gallery and live results) - a deliberate choice to avoid injecting raw HTML from an LLM response, but it means Claude's markdown-formatted answers show literal '**bold**' asterisks and '# Header' hashes instead of rendering, and URLs (now that houstory-96t.6's web search returns real ones) aren't clickable. Needs a SAFE, limited markdown-to-HTML step - not raw innerHTML of Claude's output - e.g. a small allowlist renderer handling just **bold**, ## headers, and auto-linking bare URLs (target=_blank, rel=noopener), still escaping everything else. A minimal hand-rolled linkifier is probably safer and lighter than pulling in a full markdown library for this scope. Touches the same card-rendering code as houstory-96t.31 (collapsible cards) - worth sequencing together to avoid touching the same markup twice.
close_reason: Added a safe markdown-lite renderer (escapeHtml + bold/header/link transforms, no raw HTML from Claude ever reaches innerHTML) applied everywhere ai_description is shown: upload.html's live results and Unfiled gallery, chapter.html's photo cards and unfiled picker. Verified: bold/headers render correctly, bare URLs and markdown-style [text](url) links both become real hyperlinks, and an XSS attempt (<script>alert(1)</script>) is correctly escaped rather than executed.

title: Houstory logo
description: Five Wonders' homepage uses five-wonders-logo.png (C:/code/five-wonders/five-wonders-logo.png) as its brand mark; index.html is currently just a plain text 'Houstory' heading. Needs actual artwork first - there's no image-generation tool available in this coding session, so this needs either Pete providing/commissioning art, or a separate design tool/session to produce it. Once art exists: wire it into index.html and the shared nav (houstory-96t.28, once built) in place of the text heading.
close_reason: Pete provided the logo artwork (image generated elsewhere, saved to C:/code/houstory/houstory-logo.png). Wired into index.html in place of the plain-text 'Houstory' heading, matching Five Wonders' logo pattern (centered flex wrapper, max-width 260px, .hs-logo-wrap/.hs-logo-img in houstory.css). File loads correctly (verified via curl and server access logs - 200 OK on every request); the local preview browser pane intermittently failed to fetch the ~800KB file through its tunnel, but that's a local testing-tool limitation, not a real bug - the production site is served via GitHub Pages/CDN, not this local setup.

title: Site-wide responsive navigation matching fivewonders.app
description: Right now each page (index/login/app/upload/chapter) has only a bare '<- Back' link or nothing - no consistent nav. Build shared navigation matching Five Wonders' pattern (C:/code/five-wonders/index.html): a hamburger button (.fw-hamburger) toggling a nav panel (.fw-header-nav) - check five-wonders' CSS for the exact mobile-vs-desktop breakpoint/behavior split, since Pete wants this to genuinely differ by screen size, not just be a hamburger everywhere. Houstory has no shared JS/CSS file today (each page inlines its own styles, matching the existing per-page convention) - continuing that (duplicating nav markup/CSS per page) vs introducing a shared include is a real convention change worth flagging explicitly, not deciding unilaterally. Needs real destinations: Home, Analyze (upload.html), and eventually Profile - Profile can link to a placeholder or be omitted until houstory-96t.11's profile page exists.

title: Homepage doesn't link forward to app/analyze/chapters, or reflect signed-in state
description: index.html only has a 'Sign in' link to login.html - no direct path to app.html/upload.html/chapter.html, and it doesn't check whether the visitor is already signed in (login.html itself already does this check and bounces to app.html). Fix: have index.html check the session on load and show 'Go to your home' (linking to app.html) if already signed in, 'Sign in' otherwise. Internal navigation between app.html/upload.html/chapter.html is already fine - this is specifically about the homepage's entry point.
close_reason: index.html now checks session on load: shows 'Go to your home' -> app.html when signed in, 'Sign in' -> login.html otherwise. Verified both states in browser.

title: Multi-view single-item capture (analyze grouped photos together)
description: Some items need multiple photos to fully capture - e.g. an appliance's main photo plus a photo of its model/serial sticker, or a paint can's front label plus lid. Today each uploaded photo is analyzed independently by Claude with no awareness of other photos, so info that's split across photos (brand visible in one, model number only visible in the sticker close-up) never gets combined. Let the user mark 2+ photos as views of the same item (during upload or in the needs-review queue) so they're sent to Claude together in one call, producing one merged description + fields set instead of N disconnected ones. Needs: a UI way to group photos before/at review time, and analyze-media (or a variant) accepting multiple images per request.
close_reason: Multi-view grouping built: upload.html lets you check 2+ selected files and group them as one item before uploading; analyze-media accepts media_ids (array) and sends all images to Claude in one call via a new categorize_photo_group tool, returning one shared chapter_type/description/suggested_chapter_name/fields plus a distinguishing photo_titles array. Review UI shows a thumbnail strip with per-photo editable titles and one shared description/fields/save-to. Verified end-to-end in browser: grouped 2 photos, Claude correctly distinguished them ('Five Wonders logo' vs '...(duplicate view)'), saved both to one chapter with shared description + distinct titles. Regression-tested ungrouped single-file upload still works. Known limitation: if a group isn't confirmed in the same session, its photos resurface individually (not re-grouped) in the needs-review queue - acceptable scope cut for v1.

title: Fix profile avatar/name not backfilled on existing profile row
description: ensureProfile() in app.html only seeded first_name/last_name/avatar_url from Google user_metadata when INSERTing a brand-new profiles row. If a profiles row already existed (e.g. created earlier via email/password sign-in, which has no metadata to seed from), a later Google sign-in for the same linked account skipped seeding entirely, leaving avatar_url null forever. Found via Pete testing houstory-96t.11 end-to-end: profile page showed correct name (from earlier manual test edit) but no photo. Fix: on an existing row, backfill only the fields that are still empty from user_metadata, instead of skipping.
notes: Fixed in app.html's ensureProfile(). Related to houstory-96t.11 (Google sign-in).
close_reason: Fixed in app.html ensureProfile() - now backfills empty fields on existing profile rows instead of skipping.

title: Phase 2: Google account sign-in
description: Add Google OAuth sign-in, replacing the current email+password workaround. Reuse the pattern already working in Five Wonders (C:/code/five-wonders/index.html): sb.auth.signInWithOAuth({provider:'google', options:{redirectTo:...}}), plus on first sign-in, insert a profiles row if one doesn't exist yet. Needs: (a) a profiles table (Houstory doesn't have one - currently just auth.users + properties/property_members, no user-facing profile data at all); (b) a profile page to view/edit it; (c) the Google provider configured in HOUSTORY's own Supabase project (Auth > Providers > Google) with its own Google Cloud OAuth client - Five Wonders' credentials are scoped to fivewonders.app and can't just be reused as-is, this needs its own setup (dashboard/Google Cloud Console work, not just app code).
notes: App-side code complete and committed (ccb1cf6): profiles table, profile.html, login.html Google button, ensureProfile() auto-seed in app.html. Verified in-browser end-to-end - clicking the button correctly redirects to Supabase's OAuth endpoint, which currently returns 400 'provider is not enabled'. Remaining blocker: Google provider must be enabled in Houstory's Supabase project (Auth > Providers > Google) with a Google Cloud OAuth Client ID/Secret - external dashboard config, not app code. Not closing until that's done and a real end-to-end sign-in is confirmed.
